title: As an everyday user, I can scan a QR code and immediately start generating TOTP codes for a new account
As a power user, I can keep dozens of tokens organized — search, folders or groups, and service icons — so the right code is always two taps away
As a power user, non-standard tokens work too — Steam Guard, HOTP counters, custom periods and digit lengths
As a power user, codes generate fully offline — no network, no vendor account required just to see my TOTP codes
As an everyday user, the app stores passkeys and signs me into websites and apps with them, not just TOTP codes
As a power user, my passkeys sync across ecosystems — iOS, Android, Windows, Linux, browsers — instead of being locked to one platform vendor
As a security engineer, backups are end-to-end encrypted with a key the vendor never holds, and the encryption design is documented
As an everyday user, my tokens are available on my phone, tablet, and computer at the same time, kept in sync automatically
As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device
As a power user, I can export all my TOTP secrets in an open, readable format and leave for another app whenever I choose — no lock-in
As a power user, I can import tokens in bulk from other authenticator apps instead of re-enrolling every account by hand
As an everyday user, moving to a new phone transfers all my tokens in one guided step
As an everyday user, I can read my codes from my smartwatch without pulling out my phone
As an everyday user, a browser extension autofills my TOTP codes and passkeys during login instead of making me retype them
As a power user, a first-class desktop app gives me codes and vault access on my computer, not just on mobile
As an IT admin, I can self-host the sync server on my own infrastructure and keep every secret inside my perimeter
As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed
As an everyday user, the app itself locks behind biometrics or a PIN, so a borrowed phone doesn't expose my codes
As a power user, the app warns me when a service I use is breached or a stored credential is weak, reused, or exposed
As an IT admin, push-based sign-in includes phishing defenses — number matching, location context, and admin-enforced MFA policies
As a security engineer, the vendor publishes independent security audits of the app and its sync protocol
As an IT admin, my team can share TOTP-protected logins through shared vaults or collections with per-member access control
As an IT admin, I can enforce org-wide policies — require app lock, restrict export, mandate strong master credentials — across every member's app
As an AI-native user, an agent can fetch a current TOTP code programmatically — via CLI or API — to complete a 2FA login inside an automated workflow
As an AI-native user, an agent can create and update vault entries — seeding new TOTP secrets, storing credentials — through documented programmatic surfaces
As an AI-native user, I can expose the vault through a local programmatic endpoint an agent can query for codes and secrets without screen-scraping the app
